newsitem.title: UK: Britain arranges flights out of Freetown.
newsitem.headline: Britain arranges flights out of Freetown.

text.p: LONDON - Britain is to arrange a charter flight to take Britons and other nationals out of Sierra Leone after the military coup in the West African state, the Foreign Office said on Thursday.

"Because of uncertainties about the operations of scheduled airlines, we have arranged a charter flight out of Freetown for a number of Britons and other nations who have said they want to leave," the spokesman said.
The flight is expected to leave Freetown early in the afternoon and fly to London's Gatwick airport.
There are about 800 British nationals living in Sierra Leone, some of whom have been the victims of looting. They were urged by the Foreign Office after the weekend coup to remain in their homes.
